newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi calls for more efforts to find Saudis jobs.
newsitem.headline: Saudi calls for more efforts to find Saudis jobs.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Interior Minister Prince Nayef called for increased efforts to replace foreigners with Saudi nationals in the kingdom's workforce, the official Saudi news agency SPA said.

Prince Nayef was addressing the weekly meeting of the consultative Shura Council late on Sunday which debated the issue of "Saudization", Saudi Arabia's bid to increase the number of Saudis employed in the private and public sectors.

"(Prince Nayef) emphasised the importance of unifying government and private sector efforts to offer Saudis the opportunity to serve their homeland," the council's secretary general Hamud bin Abdul-Aziz al-Badr said in a statement to SPA.
Badr also said the interior minister stressed the need for universities and colleges to prepare Saudis to do the work currently performed by expatriates.
"His highness said that it was important for individuals and companies to contribute in order to achieve the Saudization plan, which has become a pressing national issue," the secretary general said.
Saudi Arabia's 1995-2000 development plan set a target of creating 659,900 jobs for Saudis by the end of the century.

About six million expatriates work in the kingdom, which has a population of about 18 million. Analysts estimate that less than seven percent of private sector employees are Saudi and some economists put unemployment as high as 20 percent. About half the population is under the age of 20.
Saudi citizens had for decades favoured well-paid, half-day managerial jobs in the state sector. But the government can no longer create more public sector jobs to employ them.
